description:
Executes a given command in a bash shell with an optional time limit.

The shell is a bash interpreter that runs inside the run. Its commands are built in: there are no external programs such as git, npm, or docker, and no network.

- Each call starts a new shell at the root of the run's files. A `cd`, a variable, or a function lasts for that call alone.
- Chain dependent commands with `&&` in one call.
- The Shell calls of one reply run one after another, in the order listed.
- The shell reads and changes the run's files. No file has an execute bit: run a script with `bash script.sh`.
- Output past {output_cap} characters is cut in the middle: the result keeps the start and the end and says so.

working_directory.description: The absolute path to the working directory to execute the command in (defaults to the root of the run's files)

block_until_ms.description: How long to wait for the command to complete before stopping it (in milliseconds). Defaults to {timeout_ms}ms, and a larger value is lowered to that. The shell has no background, so a command that is stopped does not go on running.

description.description: Very short phrase naming what this command does; shown to the user after the word "Ran". Avoid leading with verbs or using trailing periods
